on run argv -- 1 - No One -- 2 - Contact Only -- 3 - Everyone set discoverabilityLevel to 0
-- repeat with arg in argv -- argv is a list {}, even if there is only one argument -- displayMsg(arg, missing value) -- end repeat
set argc to count argv
if argc > 1 then error "Too many arguments provided, expected only one (discoverability level)" end if
if argc is 0 then set discoverabilityLevel to 1 else set discoverabilityLevel to first item of argv end if
applyDiscoverabilityLevel(discoverabilityLevel)
return -- otherwise it will also print the last command end run
on applyDiscoverabilityLevel(discoverabilityLevel) -- there is no list of integers in AppleScript, so need to cast to string and check in a list of strings if discoverabilityLevel as string is not in {"1", "2", "3"} then set msg to "Wrong value, discoverability level can be only 1, 2 or 3" displayMsg(msg, missing value) error msg end if -- for some reason need to explicitly cast it to integer, otherwise click won't actually click set discoverabilityLevel to discoverabilityLevel as integer
-- check if user configured toggling off Bluetooth as well set toggleOffBluetooth to (system attribute "TOGGLE_OFF_BLUETOOTH") as integer
-- first set desired AirDrop discoverability level toggleAirDropViaMenuBar(discoverabilityLevel)
-- and then optionally disable Bluetooth if discoverabilityLevel is 1 and toggleOffBluetooth is 1 then toggleBluetoothOff() end if end applyDiscoverabilityLevel
on toggleAirDropViaMenuBar(discoverabilityLevel) tell application "System Events" tell process "ControlCenter" try -- via Menu Bar icon first -- check if user has added AirDrop to Menu Bar -- ( -- disabled, this worked up to Mac OS 26, but with Mac OS 27.2.1 the Menu Bar icons -- are not in the ControlCenter process anymore, see `clickMenuBarIcon()` -- ) -- set mbiAirDrop to a reference to first item of (get menu bar items of menu bar 1) whose description is "AirDrop" -- if mbiAirDrop exists then -- -- log "[DEBUG] Found AirDrop icon on Menu Bar" -- click mbiAirDrop -- else -- error "There is no AirDrop icon on Menu Bar, you need to add it there first" -- end if if not (my clickMenuBarIcon("com.apple.menuextra.airdrop")) then error "There is no AirDrop icon on Menu Bar, you need to add it there first" end if
-- no IDs or labels, have to rely on ordinals my waitForElement(a reference to first checkbox of group 1 of window "Control Centre") set tglAirDrop to first checkbox of group 1 of window "Control Centre" if discoverabilityLevel is 1 then tell tglAirDrop if (its value as boolean) then click tglAirDrop end tell else tell tglAirDrop if not (its value as boolean) then click tglAirDrop end tell
-- the level options only appear once AirDrop is on my waitForElement(a reference to checkbox discoverabilityLevel of group 1 of window "Control Centre") set tglAirDropDiscoverability to checkbox discoverabilityLevel of group 1 of window "Control Centre" tell tglAirDropDiscoverability if not (its value as boolean) then click tglAirDropDiscoverability end tell end if on error ex -- fallback to Control Centre -- log "[DEBUG] " & ex try -- disabled, see comments on clicking checkbox 4 below -- -- set mbiControlCentre to a reference to first item of (get menu bar items of menu bar 1) whose description is "Control Centre" -- if mbiControlCentre exists then -- click mbiControlCentre -- else -- error "Couldn't find Control Centre on Menu Bar" -- end if -- -- no IDs or labels, have to rely on ordinals -- checkbox 4 is the AirDrop icon item, which just toggles the state ON and OFF -- without openning options, but we want to click on the text, because then -- the options menu will appear, and that is not possible to do through Accessibility -- -- TODO: when this menu becomes accessible, implement logic for setting desired state instead of the current "dumb" toggling -- click checkbox 4 of group 1 of window "Control Centre" -- error "AirDrop options menu is not available through Accessibility, falling back to Finder window" on error ex -- log "[DEBUG] " & ex my toggleAirDropViaFinder(discoverabilityLevel) return -- otherwise it will get to pressing ESC below end try end try
key code 53 -- ESC end tell end tell end toggleAirDropViaMenuBar
on toggleAirDropViaFinder(discoverabilityLevel) tell application "Finder" make new Finder window activate end tell
tell application "System Events" to tell process "Finder" keystroke "R" using {command down, shift down} -- -- check if Bluetooth is disabled -- ( -- looks like this isn't needed anymore starting with Mac OS 15.5 Sequoia, because it is turned on regardless, -- so this step is redundant -- ) -- set bluetoothButton to a reference to (first button of splitter group 1 of window 1) -- neither of these works: whose name is "Turn On Bluetooth" / whose value of attribute "Title" is "Turn On Bluetooth" -- if bluetoothButton exists then -- -- for some reason cannot put both of these conditions into one if statement -- if discoverabilityLevel is not 1 then -- click bluetoothButton -- else -- -- Bluetooth is off and selected discoverability level is 1, won't enable Bluetooth then -- tell application "Finder" -- close first window -- end tell -- return -- end if -- end if -- -- open the "Allow me to be discovered by" dropdown -- ( -- starting with Mac OS 15.5 Sequoia this went to shit, because in different situations, which I could not -- establish which is which, the button ID might `2` or it might be `1`, and what's amazing is that -- if you'll first check for the existence of the button `1`, then it fucking will be existing, -- though the "correct" button will be actually `2` (as if they both exist at that same moment, -- but one is hidden or something), so this is fucked, but luckly if you do the check the other way around, -- so first you check for the existence of the button `2`, then it will correctly get that it does not exist -- and will fallback to button `1`, what is the actual fuck -- ) -- ( -- disabled, this worked up to Mac OS 26, but with Mac OS 27.2.1 the dropdown is not a button anymore -- ) -- set discoverabilityButton to a reference to (button 2 of group 1 of splitter group 1 of splitter group 1 of window 1) -- -- it is also cute how you can do `if discoverabilityButton exists then` for negative condition you need to do this -- if not (exists discoverabilityButton) then -- set discoverabilityButton to a reference to (button 1 of group 1 of splitter group 1 of splitter group 1 of window 1) -- end if -- click discoverabilityButton -- -- -- select the discoverability level -- click button discoverabilityLevel of group 1 of pop over 1 of group 1 of splitter group 1 of splitter group 1 of window 1 -- -- ( -- with Mac OS 27.2.1 the dropdown is a pop up button with a menu instead of a button with a pop over, -- and when Bluetooth is off the same group also has an unlabelled button (next to the -- "Turn on Bluetooth to share with AirDrop." text), which is probably what made the button ordinals -- above so confusing on Mac OS 15.5; addressing the pop up button by its own class doesn't depend -- on that, and waiting for it covers the AirDrop view not being loaded yet right after the keystroke -- ) set discoverabilityPopUp to a reference to (pop up button 1 of group 1 of splitter group 1 of splitter group 1 of window 1) my waitForElement(discoverabilityPopUp) click discoverabilityPopUp
-- select the discoverability level, menu items are in the same order: No One, Contacts Only, Everyone set discoverabilityMenu to a reference to (menu 1 of discoverabilityPopUp) my waitForElement(discoverabilityMenu) click menu item discoverabilityLevel of discoverabilityMenu
-- close current Finder window, otherwise they'll spam the user eventually tell application "Finder" close first window end tell end tell end toggleAirDropViaFinder
on toggleBluetoothOff() tell application "System Events" tell process "ControlCenter" try -- via Menu Bar icon first -- check if user has added Bluetooth to Menu Bar -- ( -- disabled, this worked up to Mac OS 26, see `toggleAirDropViaMenuBar()` -- ) -- set mbiBluetooth to a reference to first item of (get menu bar items of menu bar 1) whose description is "Bluetooth" -- if mbiBluetooth exists then -- -- log "[DEBUG] Found Bluetooth icon on Menu Bar" -- click mbiBluetooth -- else -- error "There is no Bluetooth icon on Menu Bar, you need to add it there first" -- end if if not (my clickMenuBarIcon("com.apple.menuextra.bluetooth")) then error "There is no Bluetooth icon on Menu Bar, you need to add it there first" end if
-- no IDs or labels, have to rely on ordinals my waitForElement(a reference to first checkbox of group 1 of window "Control Centre") set tglBluetooth to first checkbox of group 1 of window "Control Centre" tell tglBluetooth if (its value as boolean) then click tglBluetooth end tell on error ex -- fallback to Control Centre -- log "[DEBUG] " & ex -- ( -- disabled, this worked up to Mac OS 26, see `toggleAirDropViaMenuBar()` -- ) -- set mbiControlCentre to a reference to first item of (get menu bar items of menu bar 1) whose description is "Control Centre" -- if mbiControlCentre exists then -- click mbiControlCentre -- else -- -- there is no fallback for this scenario, so the script should fail -- error "Couldn't find Control Centre on Menu Bar" -- end if if not (my clickMenuBarIcon("com.apple.menuextra.controlcenter")) then -- there is no fallback for this scenario, so the script should fail error "Couldn't find Control Centre on Menu Bar" end if
-- ( -- disabled, this worked up to Mac OS 26, but with Mac OS 27.2.1 the Bluetooth toggle -- is inside a module group of its own, see `findControlCentreModule()` -- ) -- -- no IDs or labels, have to rely on ordinals -- set tglBluetooth to checkbox 3 of group 1 of window "Control Centre" set moduleBluetooth to my findControlCentreModule("controlcenter-bluetooth") if moduleBluetooth is 0 then -- there is no fallback for this scenario either error "Couldn't find Bluetooth in Control Centre" end if set tglBluetooth to checkbox 1 of group moduleBluetooth of group 1 of window "Control Centre" tell tglBluetooth if (its value as boolean) then click tglBluetooth end tell end try
key code 53 -- ESC end tell end tell end toggleBluetoothOff
on clickMenuBarIcon(iconId) -- ( -- with Mac OS 27.2.1 Apple's Menu Bar icons are hosted by the MenuBarAgent process instead of ControlCenter, -- each as the only menu bar item of its own group, and they have no descriptions anymore, but they do have -- identifiers, such as `com.apple.menuextra.airdrop` -- ) tell application "System Events" to tell process "MenuBarAgent" repeat with groupIndex from 1 to (count groups of menu bar 1) try set mbiId to value of attribute "AXIdentifier" of menu bar item 1 of group groupIndex of menu bar 1 on error set mbiId to missing value end try if mbiId is iconId then click menu bar item 1 of group groupIndex of menu bar 1 return true end if end repeat end tell return false end clickMenuBarIcon
on findControlCentreModule(toggleId) -- ( -- with Mac OS 27.2.1 every module in the Control Centre window is a group of its own, so ordinals -- would depend on the modules layout, but their toggles have identifiers, such as `controlcenter-bluetooth` -- ) tell application "System Events" to tell process "ControlCenter" repeat 30 times -- the window might not be there yet right after the click, so up to 3 seconds try repeat with groupIndex from 1 to (count groups of group 1 of window "Control Centre") try if value of attribute "AXIdentifier" of checkbox 1 of group groupIndex of group 1 of window "Control Centre" is toggleId then return groupIndex end try end repeat end try delay 0.1 end repeat end tell return 0 end findControlCentreModule
on waitForElement(uiElement) -- up to 3 seconds, and if it still doesn't exist by then, the following click fails with a clear enough error tell application "System Events" repeat 30 times if exists uiElement then return delay 0.1 end repeat end tell end waitForElement
on displayMsg(msg, autoCloseTimeout) if autoCloseTimeout is missing value then set autoCloseTimeout to 0 display dialog msg buttons {"OK"} default button "OK" giving up after autoCloseTimeout end displayMsg

# Alfred runs this with zsh, but it sticks to POSIX sh (no arrays, every expansion quoted), # so it can also be tested with sh/bash on a system without zsh
# unlike setting it, reading the current discoverability level needs no clicking, # because `sharingd` keeps it in its preferences as Off (No One), Contacts Only # or Everyone, and it has to be read via `defaults` (which asks `cfprefsd`), # not from the plist file, as the file might not be up to date yet # ( # that is the level which is set, so with Bluetooth or Wi-Fi off AirDrop is off # regardless, but this is deliberately not checked here, to keep it simple # ) case "$(defaults read com.apple.sharingd DiscoverableMode 2>/dev/null)" in 'Off') current=1 ;; 'Contacts Only') current=2 ;; 'Everyone') current=3 ;; *) current=0 ;; esac
# one of the discoverability levels: 1 - level number (the arg for the AppleScript), 2 - title, 3 - icon printLevel() { if [ "$1" = "$current" ]; then subtitle=',"subtitle":"(current level)"' else subtitle='' fi printf '{"title":"%s","arg":"%s","icon":{"path":"List Filter Images/%s"}%s}' "$2" "$1" "$3" "$subtitle" }
# no item has an uid and Alfred's knowledge is skipped, so the items are always shown in this order printf '{"skipknowledge":true,"items":[' printLevel 1 'No One' '672de59c8c51c4a6760777b5a879b90a42c539bc.png' printf ',' printLevel 2 'Contacts Only' 'e62c361375a80746299a23f07df50cf24b675025.png' printf ',' printLevel 3 'Everyone' 'a0dbdb47e4f7baa66d895f3acbf6cecc48746b72.png' printf ']}\n'
Setting "No One" also toggles off Bluetooth
If this checkbox is set, then when you select "No One" discoverability level, the Bluetooth will be toggled off as well
